title: Grade 2 Math — Thu, Jun 26
description: Money — Day 4 of 5: Shopping problems — total cost and change
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A biscuit costs ₹5 and a juice costs ₹10. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: ₹5 + ₹10 = ₹15. The biscuit and juice together cost fifteen rupees.

questions.question: Anu buys a candy for ₹2 and a chocolate for ₹8. How much did she spend?
questions.explanation: ₹2 + ₹8 = ₹10. Anu spent ten rupees in total.

questions.question: Vikas has ₹20. He buys an apple for ₹6. How much change does he get?
questions.explanation: ₹20 − ₹6 = ₹14. Vikas gets fourteen rupees as change.

questions.question: A ruler costs ₹5 and a notebook costs ₹10. You give ₹20. How much change do you get?
A shopkeeper has items: pen ₹3, pencil ₹2. What is the total if you buy both?
questions.explanation: ₹3 + ₹2 = ₹5. A pen and pencil together cost five rupees.

questions.question: Mala buys 2 ice creams at ₹10 each. How much does she pay in all?
questions.explanation: 2 × ₹10 = ₹20. Two ice creams at ten rupees each cost twenty rupees total.

questions.question: Sam buys a ball for ₹25 and gives the shopkeeper ₹50. How much change does he get?
questions.explanation: ₹50 − ₹25 = ₹25. Sam gets twenty-five rupees as change.

questions.question: A mango costs ₹12 and a banana costs ₹4. Rita buys both. She gives ₹20. What is her change?
3 bangles cost ₹5 each. How much do all 3 bangles cost?
questions.explanation: 3 × ₹5 = ₹15. Three bangles at five rupees each cost fifteen rupees.

questions.question: Gaurav has ₹45. He buys a toy for ₹32. Can he also buy a book for ₹10?
options: No, he has no money left
questions.explanation: After the toy: ₹45 − ₹32 = ₹13. Since ₹13 > ₹10, yes he can buy the book.

questions.question: In a shop: eraser ₹3, sharpener ₹5, pencil ₹4. What is the total for all three items?
questions.explanation: ₹3 + ₹5 + ₹4 = ₹12. All three items together cost twelve rupees.

questions.question: A shopkeeper charges ₹8 for bread and ₹12 for butter. A customer gives ₹25. What change is returned?
Seema buys 4 candies at ₹3 each. She pays with a ₹20 note. How much change does she get?
questions.explanation: 4 × ₹3 = ₹12. Change = ₹20 − ₹12 = ₹8. Seema gets eight rupees back.

questions.question: Raj wants to buy: pencil ₹4, eraser ₹3 and ruler ₹8. He has ₹20. Does he have enough money and how much will be left?
questions.explanation: Total = ₹4 + ₹3 + ₹8 = ₹15. He has ₹20, so he has enough. Change = ₹20 − ₹15 = ₹5.

questions.question: A fruit shop sells: apple ₹15, orange ₹10, banana ₹5. Neha buys one of each and pays ₹50. What is her change?
